content.title: Sequential Route Changes | Layered Defense to a Vertical Finish
content.summary: First fix the relationship between the court, the ball and the basket, allowing the ball holder to continuously pass through multiple layers of visible defensive doors, using different route changes each time to solve the space problem; in the end, only perform one vertical basket action, and use crowd reaction and shared court to end it.

quick_start.input_format: Stabilize the subject and handheld object + fixed end point + at least 3 visible space doors + different route changes each time + single vertical finish + reaction final state without fictitious score
quick_start.recommended_input: The orbiting greenhouse express drone carries a luminous seed capsule, which is lowered, changed and rolled sideways through three different wind curtains. It only uses the final updraft to complete an upper docking; two botanists react through the window, and no score or victory words appear at the end.
required_anchors: Establish one stable carrier, handled token and fixed terminal goal before escalation.
Use at least three visible spatial gates, each requiring a different route change.
Use the last route opening for one decisive vertical terminal action.
End on visible witness reaction and shared geography without asserting an unshown numerical result.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.

Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: First fix the relationship between the court, the ball and the basket, allowing the ball holder to continuously pass through multiple layers of visible defensive doors, using different route changes each time to solve the space problem; in the end, only perform one vertical basket action, and use crowd reaction and shared court to end it.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.

Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Build a short action proof around successive spatial gates: establish one carrier, one handled token and a fixed terminal goal; let each visible blocker force a different route change while preserving shared geography; convert the final opening into one decisive vertical terminal action; then hold a separate witness reaction without inventing an unshown numerical result.

invariants.rule: Establish one stable carrier, handled token and fixed terminal goal before escalation.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without all three anchors, later movement reads as disconnected athletic montage.

invariants.rule: Use at least three visible spatial gates, each requiring a different route change.
invariants.purpose: Turns progression into spatial problem solving.
invariants.ablation_failure: Repeated identical dodges do not create escalating proof.

invariants.rule: Preserve the carrier, token and terminal direction across every route change.
invariants.ablation_failure: Losing the token or goal axis breaks the causal route.

invariants.rule: Use the last route opening for one decisive vertical terminal action.
invariants.purpose: Converts horizontal escalation into a readable payoff transition.
invariants.ablation_failure: Multiple terminal attempts diffuse the climax.

invariants.rule: End on visible witness reaction and shared geography without asserting an unshown numerical result.
invariants.ablation_failure: A scoreboard or victory claim would exceed the visible proof.

instantiations.concept: In an orbital greenhouse, one compact medical courier drone carries a luminous seed capsule through three moving wind-curtain gates. It changes height, lane and body angle, then uses the final updraft once to dock the capsule in an overhead sterile intake while two botanists visibly react.

instantiations.concept: In a stop-motion paper theatre, one clockwork courier carries a brass message bead through three independently moving scenery gates.
